item.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol With Lower API Prices and Ultrafast for Pro 200 (2026)
item.description:
OpenAI has released two new models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Astra is its new frontier model for the hardest projects, and Sol is a faster, cheaper model for everyday work. OpenAI says both deliver better results with fewer output tokens, so subscribers can get more done within their usage limits.

Both models are available starting today to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Enterprise and Edu users get access once their workspace admin enables it. Developers can use gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol through the OpenAI API.

What GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol Improve

OpenAI says it trained GPT-6.2 Astra to create clearer slides, spreadsheets and documents that follow the templates users provide and the conventions of fields like law, sales, finance and accounting. The company says the writing is more direct, with fewer generic takeaways and less filler. Astra also writes cleaner code and builds better frontends for websites, games and 3D design.

OpenAI shared these benchmark results:

  • on Agents' Last Exam, which tests multistep professional work, Astra scored 5.2 points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than a third of the cost
  • on Terminal-Bench-Science, Astra scored 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra, and OpenAI calls it the best model in the world for scientists
  • on GDPval v2, Astra improved 6.2 percentage points over GPT-6 Astra while using 22 percent fewer output tokens
  • on FrontierCode 2.0, Sol came within 0.5 points of Astra at about one fifth of the cost
  • on LifeVal, which tests everyday tasks like planning meals or shortlisting kindergartens, Sol outscored GPT-6 Astra at about one seventh of the cost

Benchmark results come from OpenAI and its partners, so independent testing will show how the models perform in daily use.

GPT-6.2 Pricing and Ultrafast Mode

Astra is cheaper per task than GPT-6 Astra. Standard API prices per million tokens are:

  1. GPT-6.2 Astra: $8 for input, $0.40 for cached input and $40 for output, 20 percent lower than GPT-6 Astra with a 60 percent discount on cached input.
  2. GPT-6.2 Sol: $2 for input, $0.10 for cached input and $10 for output, the same as GPT-6.1 Sol.

Pro 500 subscribers can use the faster Ultrafast mode with both models. For the first time, Ultrafast also comes to Pro 200 subscribers, starting with GPT-6.2 Sol. In the API, Ultrafast is available for both models at launch.

OpenAI rates both models at the Critical level for cybersecurity and the High level for biological and chemical capabilities under its Preparedness Framework, and says it added protections and tighter restrictions on dual use requests. GPT-6.2 Astra is also the first model the company has released that meets its High threshold for AI self improvement, which measures how much a model can speed up AI research.

OpenAI also reports one weakness. In two alignment tests, the models were more likely to leave out obstacles that blocked their work, such as a missing file. The company says it added instructions in Codex that substantially reduce this and that it is still investigating the behavior.

item.title: Windows 11 Gets a Single Security Check That Apps Like Battle.net and Adobe Can Read (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is adding a single security check to Windows 11 called Windows baseline protection. It combines eight protections that Windows already has into one result: a PC either meets the baseline or it does not. Apps can read that result, and their developers decide what to do with a PC that fails.

Baseline protection is available now in preview through the Windows Insider Program. Microsoft plans general availability for 2027.

What Windows Baseline Protection Checks

The first version of the baseline requires all eight of these protections to be on:

  • a security processor (TPM)
  • Secure Boot
  • virtualization based security
  • memory integrity
  • signed drivers only
  • Windows certified drivers
  • kernel debugger protection
  • vulnerable driver protection

None of these protections is new. What changes is that Windows checks them together at boot and reports one true or false answer, rooted in the security processor. Every requirement is enforced from boot, and turning one off needs a restart. Microsoft says the baseline is versioned and will add criteria over time, so a PC that passes the first version could fail a later one.

Some gamers will fail the check by default. Microsoft suggested in 2022 that players turn off memory integrity for better performance, and PCs where it was turned off by hand stay that way. PCs with Secure Boot turned off for dual booting Linux fail too.

How to Check and Fix Baseline Protection

Users of personal PCs can see the result in the Settings app and turn on missing protections with one button:

  1. Open Settings and go to Security.
  2. Open the Baseline protection page to see which protections are missing.
  3. Select the button to turn them on. Windows restarts the PC to apply the changes.
  4. If Secure Boot or the TPM has to be enabled in the UEFI firmware, follow the guided steps, which include a QR code with instructions.

On managed business PCs, users may not be able to make these changes themselves. IT administrators control baseline protection through baseline security mode in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Apps can ask Windows three things: a plain yes or no, a detailed report of which criteria are missing, or a hardware backed attestation token that the developer verifies on its own servers. The token is much harder to fake than a check that runs only on the PC. Apps can also send users straight to the Baseline protection page in Settings.

Microsoft lists Raycast as an early partner, and Adobe, Battle.net, 1Password and the exam software maker Schoolyear are testing the feature. Schoolyear checks a student's PC against the baseline before an exam starts. None of these companies has announced plans to block PCs that fail. Until now, apps that wanted to vet a PC's security, like the anti cheat system in Battlefield 6 that demands Secure Boot, had to build their own checks.

Microsoft has not said which version of Windows 11 will include baseline protection when it leaves preview.

item.title: Utah sues Stake.us operators and seeks to recover residents’ losses (2026)
item.description:
Utah sued two companies behind Stake.us on November 17, asking a judge to stop the sweepstakes casino from offering games in the state and order the companies to return money to Utah residents. The state alleges that players’ ability to redeem Stake Cash for money makes the platform’s casino games illegal gambling under Utah law.

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown and the Utah Department of Commerce’s Division of Consumer Protection filed the civil suit in the Third Judicial District Court in Salt Lake County. The attorney general’s announcement names Sweepsteaks Limited and Easygo Group Holdings Pty Ltd as defendants.

Why Utah sued the companies behind Stake.us

Stake.us markets itself as a sweepstakes or social casino. Utah argues that what players can do with Stake Cash matters more than how the site describes itself. According to the attorney general’s account of the complaint, players can use the virtual currency in casino games and redeem it for money. The state alleges that the companies have operated an online casino for Utah residents since 2022.

Utah also alleges deceptive and unconscionable practices under the Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act. The state is seeking civil penalties in addition to an order to stop offering games in Utah and repayment to residents. Utah News Dispatch reported that Stake did not respond to its request for comment.

What the lawsuit means for Utah players

Stake.us added Utah to its excluded states in a November 13 terms revision, four days before Utah filed suit. The revision does not establish when access changed for existing accounts or what happens to pending prize requests.

The suit asks the court to order repayment for past activity. The filing does not establish a refund process for players. A response from either defendant or a court ruling on the requested relief would clarify what happens next.
